title: Halle Berry’s Lawyer Slams Olivier Martinez’s Abuse Claims, Defends Actress Amid Son Allegations
body:
Hollywood’s most closely watched custody battle took another dramatic turn on Thursday when a Los Angeles judge issued a temporary restraining order against Oscar‑winning actress Halle Berry. The order, requested by Berry’s former partner Olivier Martinez, also grants him sole physical custody of their 11‑year‑old son, Mace. Martinez’s petition alleges that Berry physically abused their child, including a claim that she once choked him during an argument. Berry’s legal team responded immediately, dismissing the accusations as “meritless” and demanding that the court examine the lack of evidence behind the allegations.

Martinez, a former model and actor who has been in a long‑term relationship with Berry since 2012, filed the emergency motion after a series of heated exchanges that reportedly escalated into a physical confrontation. In his filing, Martinez asserted that Berry’s “aggressive behavior” placed Mace in danger and that he could no longer allow the child to remain in the actress’s care. The temporary restraining order bars Berry from having any unsupervised contact with Mace and requires her to stay at least 500 feet away from Martinez’s residence and workplace until a full hearing can be scheduled.

Berry’s attorney, attorney‑general‑level litigator D. Michele Bennett, issued a statement shortly after the court’s decision, labeling the accusations “baseless” and “designed to manipulate the legal process.” Bennett said the family has “never witnessed any form of physical discipline that could be construed as abuse” and that the claim of choking is “completely unfounded.” The lawyer also warned that Martinez’s actions could be part of a broader strategy to gain leverage in an ongoing dispute over the child’s primary residence, which has been a point of contention since the couple’s split in 2023.

Legal experts note that temporary restraining orders in family‑law cases are often granted on a “best‑interest‑of‑the‑child” standard, which can be satisfied by any credible claim of danger, even if the evidence is preliminary. “The court’s primary concern is to protect the child while it gathers more information,” said family‑law attorney Rebecca Liu of the Los Angeles Bar Association. “A temporary order does not equate to a finding of guilt; it simply freezes the status quo until a thorough investigation can be conducted.” Liu added that high‑profile cases like this one are especially scrutinized, as public pressure can influence both parties’ willingness to settle out of court.

The allegations have also reignited a broader conversation about how celebrity custody disputes are handled in the public eye. In recent years, several high‑profile families have faced similar accusations, ranging from claims of neglect to allegations of emotional abuse, often magnified by relentless media coverage. Critics argue that the intense spotlight can impede a fair legal process, while supporters contend that public awareness can safeguard vulnerable children. Media ethicist Dr. Samuel Kline observes that “the line between legitimate concern for a child’s welfare and sensationalism is thin, and journalists must tread carefully to avoid prejudicing either side.”

As the case moves toward a full hearing, both parties are expected to present extensive evidence, including medical records, witness testimonies, and possibly video footage from the couple’s home security system. The court will also consider the child’s own preferences, as California law permits a child over the age of 14 to express a custody preference, though Mace is currently 11. Meanwhile, Berry’s representatives have signaled an intent to file a counter‑petition seeking joint custody and to challenge the restraining order on procedural grounds.

The unfolding drama underscores the complexities of navigating parental rights, personal safety, and public scrutiny. While the temporary order limits Berry’s access to her son for now, the ultimate determination will hinge on a detailed factual record and the court’s assessment of what arrangement best serves Mace’s emotional and physical well‑being. As both sides prepare for what could become a protracted legal battle, the entertainment world and the public alike will be watching closely to see how the story resolves and what precedent it may set for future high‑profile custody disputes.
